findings.text: the fragment states every arm above was re-run at the head as finally committed and cites logs/final-head-*.log, but those logs' headers read revision fa01f7936ddbce01b3674e2c7e566d5218e1e37a, not the final head a7cc0895e2ac; sixteen commits landed after them, including nova/imas/equilibrium.py, sample.py, pulsedesign.py and io/sourcemap.py, so six of the ten arms were not measured at the head the sentence names, although each of the six exercises a module no later commit touched.

the head column reports tests/test_database.py at 94.72 s and, at :125, tests/test_pointconstraint.py at 7.30 s, while the logs the paragraph cites record 86.25 s and 5.01 s, so the table does not reconcile with the logs it names; the pass and skip counts do agree.

after_suite is recorded as two objects carrying an `arms` list with no exit_status, completed, failure_count or failure_ids, and a command containing <worktree>, <fresh /dev/shm dir> and <file> placeholders, so promotion cannot read a status or a failing id from it and this review derived the added-failure delta from the per-arm logs instead.

changed_paths omits nova/imas/metadata.py, nova/io/sourcemap.py, tests/test_metadata.py, tests/test_sample_write_convention.py and docs/evidence/fragments/dd-cocos-ingest/dd-internal-sites.html, all five changed in the diff and all five inside the scope the repair rounds granted, so the record understates the change a coordinator is promoting.

load() implements "refuse a cache entry whose stored COCOS convention is unknown or foreign" as a dataset attrs marker plus eviction, a capability nova/io/signalstore.py:82-133 already owns by keying the group name on the convention (cache_key, legacy_cache_key, stale_group, read); the addition does not extend that owner, and the two mechanisms now detect the same class of stale entry differently.

the writer's factor names the Data Dictionary version as the literal "3.39.0", while nova/imas/sample.py:22 was added in this node as DEFAULT_DD_VERSION to own exactly that default; two statements of one default in two modules can drift, and the sample writer beside it derives the version from its target instead.

the fixture docstring explains the pinned IMAS_HOME by what "happened to the coordinator", a role attribution in source where the rule is to state the mechanism that makes the two sides resolve one tree.

the assertion compares the constraint's output against the -5.0 the test itself hands the stand-in at :61, so its two sides move together by construction; its independence rests entirely on the recorded control logs/negative-control-inverse-negation-restored.log, which does redden it when the negation is restored, and the assertion carries no independent oracle of its own.
